Spider of the Week 5 - Liphistius kanthan (Kathan Cave Trapdoor Spider)

Liphistius Kanthan is a critically endanger species that lives in the Kanthan cave system in Malaysia. It shares the area of the hill with another critically endangered rare plant and an uncommon palm tree that has the greatest density on top of the hill. A limestone mining company has mining rights to the hill containing the cave so it is possible all three species might go extinct in the near future.

The Kanthan Cave Spider like other Liphistius spiders has 6-8 sensory lines leading out from its trapdoor, it will wait with its legs resting on the lines until it feels prey or an enemy cross the line. In the case of prey it will rush out and grab the prey dragging it into its nest, if it senses an enemy it will rush out from a backdoor it keeps in its nest.

The Kanthan Cave Spider builds its nest along a cave wall and then cover and camouflages the nest with mud, moss, and debris; unlike most trapdoor spiders which burrow into banks of earth or holes in trees and logs. Their nest often has one or more well hidden backdoors it can use when threatened.
